**Methods that call it directly** (each calls `EnsureNotDisposed()` itself, in `src/Polly.Core/CircuitBreaker/Controller/CircuitStateController.cs`):
- `CircuitStateController.CircuitState` (line 53)
- `CircuitStateController.LastException` (line 66)
- `CircuitStateController.LastHandledOutcome` (line 79)
- `CircuitStateController.IsolateCircuitAsync` (line 90)
- `CircuitStateController.CloseCircuitAsync` (line 110)
- `CircuitStateController.OnActionPreExecuteAsync` (line 126)
- `CircuitStateController.OnUnhandledOutcomeAsync` (line 196)
- `CircuitStateController.OnHandledOutcomeAsync` (line 222)

**Methods that reach it only indirectly:**
- `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy.ExecuteCore` (`src/Polly.Core/CircuitBreaker/CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy.cs:32`) calls `OnActionPreExecuteAsync`. It also calls `OnHandledOutcomeAsync` (line 52) and `OnUnhandledOutcomeAsync` (line 56).
- The `CircuitBreakerResilienceStrategy` constructor (lines 18–21) hands `CircuitState`, `IsolateCircuitAsync` and `CloseCircuitAsync` to the state provider and manual control. Those reach `EnsureNotDisposed` when invoked, but the graph does not list the constructor as a caller.

**Test file:**
- `test/Polly.Core.Tests/CircuitBreaker/Controller/CircuitStateControllerTests.cs`. The graph counts 35 tests in it that reach the method. One example is line 167, which asserts `ObjectDisposedException` from `IsolateCircuitAsync`.

**Gaps:**
- The graph flagged 9 call sites it could not attribute, because 40 symbols share the name `EnsureNotDisposed`. They are in `DelegatingComponent.cs`, `BridgeComponent.cs`, `BridgeComponent.TResult.cs`, `CompositeComponent.cs`, `HedgingResilienceStrategyTests.cs` and `CompositeComponentBenchmark.cs`. Those files are in the pipeline and hedging code, so they almost certainly call other `EnsureNotDisposed` methods. I did not open them to confirm.
- The grep found no other callers of the controller inside `src/Polly.Core/CircuitBreaker`.
- I could not run a search of the test projects for other users of the controller, because the shell was denied. Other test files, such as the strategy tests, may reach `EnsureNotDisposed` indirectly through `ExecuteCore`, and the graph does not list them.

I changed no files.
